newsitem.title: UK: Tesco says current sales rise six percent.
newsitem.headline: Tesco says current sales rise six percent.

text.p: Britain's leading supermarket group Tesco Plc said on Tuesday that sales from existing stores were up six percent in the first four weeks of the current year, which excluded the Easter holiday period.

The company said year pretax profits were 750 million pounds ($1.2 billion), up from 675 million previously and in line with expectations, while it paid out a total dividend of 10.35 pence, compared with 9.8 pence.

"This is a good start in a competitive environment," the company said, adding that inflation had fallen through the second half of last year from 3.5 percent to just one percent currently. Chairman Lord MacLaurin, who steps down in June, said the results reflected Tesco's policy of offering "extremely keen prices and first-class service."

Tesco said operating margin was reduced by 0.4 percent to 5.8 percent as a strong performance in food offset the cost of a petrol price war, which impacted profits growth in the UK by about five percent and margins by 0.3 percent.

Tesco, which paid 630 million pounds for the Irish supermarkets of Associated British Foods (ABF) in March, said increasing returns from new stores and extensions had helped to increase return on capital employed to 17.1 percent from 15.7 percent in 1994.

The company said it expected to open 26 stores in the UK in the current year while it aims to add six to eight new stores in central Europe in 1998 and chairman Lord MacLaurin, who steps down after these results, said the results reflected Tesco's policy of offering "extremely keen prices and first-class service."
